title: Checks for a shebang directive in a file that is not executable.
summary: In Python, a shebang (also known as a hashbang) is the first line of a script, which specifies the interpreter that should be used to run the script. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-executable and made it stable in v0.0.233.

title: Common base class for all non-exit exceptions.
Check that match statements match exhaustively.
summary: If enabled with --enable-error-code exhaustive-match, mypy generates an error if a match statement does not match all possible cases/types. mypy does not enable this error code by default. Use --enable-error-code exhaustive-match to enable it.

title: Check the return type of __exit__.
summary: If mypy can determine that :py__exit__ always returns False, mypy checks that the return type is *not* bool. The boolean value of the return type affects which lines mypy thinks are reachable after a with statement, since any :py__exit__ method that can return True may swallow exceptions. mypy enables this error code by default.

title: Check that explicit Any type annotations are not allowed.
summary: If you use --disallow-any-explicit, mypy generates an error if you use an explicit Any type annotation. mypy does not enable this error code by default. Use --enable-error-code explicit-any to enable it.

title: Check that @override is used when overriding a base class method.
summary: If you use --enable-error-code explicit-override mypy generates an error if you override a base class method without using the @override decorator. An error will not be emitted for overrides of __init__ or __new__. See PEP 698. mypy does not enable this error code by default. Use --enable-error-code explicit-override to enable it.
